- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or use lagged mean.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope or add 1–2% buffer.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model may overcorrect; forecast should align with 10–15 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (last 7–10 days); apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5% for final 10 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model underreacts; add 0.3–0.7% adjustment to forecast slope.
